ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: Development of cold water fisheries
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Development of cold water fisheries प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 1:34PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying has been implementing a flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) with an  investment of Rs 20,050 crore in all the States/Union Territories. In order to address the infrastructure gaps in fisheries and  aquaculture, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India with effect  from the financial year 2018-19 has also been implementing a dedicated fund Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) with a fund size of Rs 7522.48 crore. The PMMSY inter alia aims to address critical gaps in fish production and productivity, quality, technology, post-harvest infrastructure and management, modernisation and strengthening of value chain, traceability, establishing a robust fisheries management framework and fishers’ welfare in cold water fisheries. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India, has approved  various fisheries developmental projects of Himalayan and Hilly States for an amount of Rs.706 crore including projects for cold water fisheries development. A framework titled Model Guidelines for the Development of Cold Water Fisheries was issued on 14 th March, 2026 to support States in developing coldwater fisheries and its associated infrastructure. These guidelines provide specifications for development of Raceways, Re-circulatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS), hatcheries, feed mills, disease prevention and market linkagesfor augmenting production, value addition and marketing of commercially important coldwater fish species like Rainbow Trout, Golden Mahseer and Snow Trout. In addition, the Department of Fisheries, Government of India has notified four clusters specifically for development of cold water fisheries at  Anant Nag District in Jammu and Kashmir,  Pithoragarh District in Uttarakhand,  Kargil District in Ladakh and  Kullu District in Himachal Pradesh. (c) and (d) : The Department of Fisheries, Government of India promotes adoption of emerging technologies such as RAS, Biofloc, Cages, IoT‑based water quality monitoring, GIS mapping, automated feeders and digital market platforms for  fish farmers in remote and mountainous regions. Under PMMSY, a model RAS for coldwater fisheries has been developed through Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)-Central Institute of Coldwater Fisheries Research (ICAR-CICFR), Bhimtal for intensive trout production and year‑round breeding of Golden Mahseer. Moreover, ICAR‑Central Institute of Fisheries Technology (CIFT) Kochi has supported fish processing and Ready‑to‑Eat facilities in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked. content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Allocation of funds under Blue Revolution प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 1:33PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India with effect from the Financial Year 2020-21 has been implementing a flagship scheme of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) for holistic development of fisheries and aquaculture sector in the country. The State/UT-wise details of fund approved and released under the PMMSY during the last three financial years (2023-24 to 2025-26) is furnished at Annexure-I. The State/UT-wise allocation of central funds under PMMSY are made on annual basis depending on the overall budgetary allocation, performance of the States/UTs, fund absorbing capacity, physical and financial progress,  liabilities created in respect of the projects approved in the previous financial years. There is no disparity in allocation of funds among the States and Union Territories under the PMMSY. The fisheries and aquaculture development projects and initiatives taken by the Department of Fisheries, Government of India under the PMMSY have contributed towards augmentation of fish production, productivity and exports. During the last five years (2020-21 to 2024-25), fish production in the country has increased from 141.64 lakh tonne in 2019-20 to 197.75 lakh tonne in 2024-25 (39.61% increase) and fisheries export from Rs.46,666 crore (2019-20) to Rs.73,890 crore (2025-26) (58.34% increase). The Department of Fisheries has developed the PMMSY Management Information System (MIS) as a centralized digital portal and dashboard utilized to track the progress of the Fisheries projects taken up under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). The MIS aggregates district and state-level data to enable monitoring and evaluation of the progress. Issuance of need based advisories, regular physical and virtual meetings with the States/UTs and field visits are undertaken to monitor and review the progress of projects and improve the effective utilization of funds. ***** Annexure-I Statement - State/UT-wise details of Central funds approved and funds released during the last three financial years (2023-24 to 2025-26) under PMMSY (Rs. in lakhs) Sl. title: Women led cooperatives in fisheries
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Women led cooperatives in fisheries प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 1:32PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the ongoing Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) supports the formation of Fisheries Cooperative Societies across the country including in the state of Andhra Pradesh.  The Government of Andhra Pradesh has informed that a total of 213 women-led coastal Cooperative Societies have been formed in the areas of fisheries, seaweed cultivation and marine processing, benefitting 27,447 beneficiaries across 12 districts, including Kakinada from 1 st April 2021 to 15 th June 2026 . The district wise details of women-led coastal cooperative societies along with the number of beneficiaries associated with them, are given at Annexure-I . (c) For the promotion and strengthening of women-led coastal fisheries cooperatives across the country, the Government of India is continuously engaging with the States and Union Territories through various schemes and programmes. As part of these efforts, fisheries cooperatives are encouraged to register on the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) and are eligible for higher incentives, including performance grants of up to ₹2 crore under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PMMKSSY). Women-led fisheries cooperatives are also accorded priority in the issuance of Access Passes for fishing in the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and Letters of Authorization (LoA) for High Seas fishing. Further, to facilitate greater participation of fisheries cooperatives in High Seas fishing, the application and renewal fee for the Letter of Authorization has been reduced from ₹25,000 to ₹5,000. (d) As a part of Blue Economy, the Department of Fisheries, through Natio nal Fisheries Development Board (NFDB), has formulated an action plan to support the formation of 12,000 fisheries cooperatives across the country, including women-led Coastal Cooperative Societies in uncovered panchayats and villages. In addition, the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Saha-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) a sub-scheme of PMMSY envisages for strengthening of 5500 Primary Fisheries Cooperative Societies across the country including women-led Fisheries Cooperative Societies, with mentoring, capacity building and need based financial support. ****** Annexure-I Statement  regarding Women led cooperatives in fisheries Sl. content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Blue Economy through reservoir and Amrit Sarovar fisheries प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 1:31PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India in the Union Budget, 2026-27 has announced the development of fisheries and aquaculture by undertaking integrated development of 500 reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars in the country. The initiative reinforces the Government’s objective to harvest the untapped fisheries potential from reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars, strengthening livelihood of fishermen in the reservoirs and engagement of women self help groups (SHGs), fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPO) for development of fisheries in Amrit Sarovars and Reservoirs. (b): The investment for the implementation of the Integrated Development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars will be based on the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) submitted by the States and Union Territories (UTs). The selection has been done in consultation with the States and UTs, considering the perennial water availability and fisheries potential of the identified reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. State and UT wise reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars identified as on date are at Annexure-I and Annexure-II respectively. (c): The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India (GoI) with the objective of enhancing fisher’s income in the country is promoting Fish Farmer Producer Organization (FFPOs), women-led groups and fisheries cooperatives under the Integrated development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. This includes the formation of new Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs), women-led groups, and fisheries cooperatives, as well as support for existing ones, in the selected reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. **** Annexure-I Statement State-wise details of identified Reservoirs for its Integrated Development S.N Name of States Total no. of reservoirs 1 Arunachal Pradesh 12 2 Bihar 12 3 Chhattisgarh 27 4 Goa 3 6 Gujarat 12 7 Himachal Pradesh 5 8 Jammu & Kashmir 4 9 Jharkhand 41 10 Karnataka 11 11 Kerala 28 12 Madhya Pradesh 22 13 Maharashtra 34 14 Manipur 4 15 Meghalaya 3 16 Mizoram 3 17 Nagaland 1 18 Odisha 25 19 Punjab 7 20 Rajasthan 15 21 Tamilnadu 10 22 Telangana 27 23 Tripura 1 24 Uttarakhand 6 25 Uttar Pradesh 19 26 Andhra Pradesh 13 27 West Bangal 6 Total 351 ****** Annexure-II Statement : State-wise details of identified Amrit Sarovars S.N Name of States Total no. of Amrit Sarovars 1 Bihar 5 2 Himachal Pradesh 4 3 Jharkhand 5 4 Meghalaya 3 5 Chhattisgarh 5 6 Madhya Pradesh 5 7 Uttarakhand 4 8 Mizoram 2 9 Kerala 4 10 Gujarat 3 11 Telangana 6 12 Uttar Pradesh 12 13 Tamilnadu 6 14 Odisha 5 15 Nagaland 5 16 Rajasthan 5 17 Tripura 5 18 Assam 5 19 Punjab 3 20 Maharashtra 6 21 Sikkim 2 Total 100 This I nformation was given by Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh in the Rajya Sabha in response to a question asked. ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: Traceability systems in seafood export
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Traceability systems in seafood export प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 1:30PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Government of India, is implementing several strategic initiatives to strengthen seafood export infrastructure under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). Under PMMSY, projects for the development of the fisheries and aquaculture sector , amounting to ₹21,394.88 crore with a Central share of ₹9,510.89 crore, have been approved, including those for the creation and strengthening of export infrastructure. Further, infrastructure has been augmented through the Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), under which 18 major projects, with a total project cost of ₹345.89 crore, have been supported, primarily for the expansion and modernization of fish processing plants. The year-wise and State-wise details of financial assistance provided under PMMSY and FIDF are enclosed at Annexure-II and Annexure-III, respectively. In addition, the MPEDA is implementing the Technology Development for Specific Value-Added Marine Products (TDSVMP) Scheme, under which financial assistance is provided for the development of value-added infrastructure. The Scheme supports the establishment and modernization of fish processing facilities, cold storage, automated processing machinery, infrastructure for handling live, chilled, ornamental , and dried fish, and the development of new value-added seafood products. During the period from 2021-22 to 2025-26, MPEDA has provided financial assistance of ₹118.10 crore to 89 seafood processing units for infrastructure development under the Scheme. The Export Inspection Council (EIC), under the Department of Commerce, is the Competent Authority for quality control and inspection of notified export products, including marine products. To ensure compliance with importing countries' requirements, EIC conducts periodic training on Food Safety Management System (FSMS) requirements for approved seafood export establishments and mandates testing of aquaculture shrimp for banned antibiotics during export certification. The MPEDA supports these efforts through pre-harvest testing, certification programmes such as SHAPHARI, and, together with the Coastal Aquaculture Authority (CAA) and EIC, implement ing the National Residue Control Plan (NRCP) to strengthen residue monitoring, traceability , and compliance with international standards. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India , supports quality enhancement and export competitiveness through the PMMSY by promoting branding, standards and certification, capacity building, post-harvest infrastructure, cold-chain facilities, and the modernization of fishing harbours and fish landing centres. The Department of Fisheries, GoIalso supports the culture of export-oriented species such as Scampi, Mud Crab, Asian Seabass , and Cobia, and promotes advanced aquaculture technologies, including Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS) and Biofloc technology. Further, the Department of Fisheries, GoI is promoting sustainable seafood production by supporting the Marine Mammal Stock Assessment Project and the fitment of Turtle Excluder Devices (TEDs) on shrimp trawl s under PMMSY. In addition, the CAA has updated the list of prohibited pharmacologically active substances and antimicrobial agents under the Coastal Aquaculture Authority Rules, 2024, to strengthen compliance with international food safety requirements. The Department of Fisheries, Government of India, has released the National Framework on Traceability in Fisheries and Aquaculture, 2025 , to establish a national digital traceability system across the fisheries and aquaculture value chain. The Framework aims to ensure compliance with domestic and international requirements, strengthen food safety, quality assurance , and transparency, enhance consumer confidence, and facilitate market access, thereby boosting seafood exports. It envisages a phased and technology-driven implementation through a National Level Governance Committee (NLGC) for strategic oversight and an Adoption Committee to facilitate the adoption of an IT-based national traceability system by fisheries and aquaculture stakeholders. title: Review of implementation of PMMSY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Review of implementation of PMMSY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 1:28PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Fisheries, Government of India (DoF, GoI), regularly reviews the implementation of projects approved under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) in all States/Union Territories(UTs) including Maharashtra through physical meetings, virtual meetings, field visits and digital monitoring through a dedicated centralized digital platform for scheme implementation. (b) and (c): Under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), during 2020-21 to 2026-27, the DoF, GoI has approved the proposals for fisheries development submitted by the Government of Maharashtra amounting to Rs. 1,601.44 crore, with central share of Rs. 593.33 crore. Out of this, central funds amounting to Rs. 419.02 crore has been released and the Government of Maharashtra has utilized Rs. 408.77 crore of this released funds. The approvals include various fisheries activities towards enhancing fish production, productivity, strengthening infrastructure facilities, development of cold chain and marketing facilities, sustainability of resources and activities towards fishermen safety and welfare. Under PMMSY, beneficiary selection and projects implementation are done by the respective State Governments/UTs. The district-wise details of important fisheries infrastructure projects implemented under PMMSY as reported by Government of Maharashtra are Annexed. (d): The Government of Maharashtra has informed total of 3714 beneficiary oriented projects are active in the State under PMMSY out of which 2856 projects are 100% completed. From these, direct employment for 15,763 persons and indirect employment opportunities for 19,528 persons are generated in the State. It is also informed that upon completion of all approved projects, the ongoing projects are expected to generate additional employment opportunities and further strengthen the socio-economic status of the fisheries sector in Maharashtra. ***** Annexure Statement re garding Review of implementation of PMMSY. ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
title: Fisheries, reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying Fisheries, reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 1:27PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India in the Union Budget, 2026-27 has announced the development of fisheries and aquaculture by undertaking integrated development of 500 reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars in the country. The initiative reinforces the Government’s objective to harvest the untapped fisheries potential from reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars, strengthening livelihood of fishermen in the reservoirs and engagement of women self help groups (SHGs), fisheries cooperatives, Fish Farmers Producer Organizations (FFPO) for development of fisheries in Amrit Sarovars and Reservoirs. The key components envisaged for implementation of such initiatives includes strengthening quality seed production by establishing hatchery, promotion of cage and pen culture in reservoir, providing boats and nets to reservoir fishermen, promotion of composite fish culture and integrated fish farming in the Amrit Sarovar, establishment of fisheries infrastructure such as fish feed mill, cold storage, ice plant, fish kiosk and retail fish market, fish transport vehicle and fish value added unit. (b): The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Government of India (GoI) in consultation with States and Union Territories (UTs) has selected 351 reservoirs and 100 Amrit Sarovars. The selection was based on the lists submitted by the States and UTs, considering the perennial water availability and fisheries potential of the identified reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. (c): The Department of Fisheries (DoF), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAH&D), Government of India (GoI) with the objective of enhancing fisher’s income in the country is promoting Fish Farmer Producer Organization (FFPOs), women-led groups and fisheries cooperatives under the Integrated development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. This includes the formation of new Fish Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs), women-led groups, and fisheries cooperatives, as well as support for existing ones, in the selected reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars. (d): The investment for the implementation of the Integrated Development of Reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars shall be based on the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) submitted by the States and Union Territories (UTs). The unit cost and funding pattern shall be as per the existing guidelines of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). title: DRI busts clandestine Mephedrone manufacturing facility in Ankleshwar, Gujarat and seizes Rs. 21 lakh; Three arrested
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Finance DRI busts clandestine Mephedrone manufacturing facility in Ankleshwar, Gujarat and seizes Rs. 21 lakh; Three arrested प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 3:43PM by PIB Delhi In a major operation, the officers of the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) successfully dismantled a clandestine Mephedrone manufacturing facility operating from a residential premises in Ankleshwar, Gujarat, and arrested three persons involved in the illicit drug manufacturing and trafficking network. In an intelligence led operation, officers of DRI unearthed a fully functional illicit laboratory equipped with sophisticated manufacturing apparatus, including an industrial oven dryer, hot plate heaters, condenser assembly, electric stirrer, and other laboratory equipment used for the clandestine manufacture of Mephedrone. The search resulted in the recovery of 1.349 kg Mephedrone in solid form, 6.825 kg 2-Bromo-4-Methylpropiophenone, a controlled precursor chemical, and 120 litres of Monomethylamine (MMA), another essential chemical used in the manufacture of Mephedrone along with 60 kg Hydrobromic Acid (HBr), 40 litres Toluene, and two containers containing mixed acids (HBr and HCl), all of which were seized under the provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act 1985. Mephedrone, commonly known on the streets as "Meow Meow", "MD", "M-Cat" or "Drone", is a highly addictive synthetic psychotropic substance that has emerged as one of the most abused stimulant drugs in India. It is notified as a psychotropic substance under the NDPS Act, 1985, making its manufacture, possession, sale, transport and trafficking illegal except for authorised scientific or medical purposes. Simultaneous searches conducted at the residential premises of the accused led to the recovery of Rs. 20 lakh, believed to be proceeds of illicit drug trafficking. In a swift follow-up operation, DRI officers apprehended the intended receiver of the manufactured contraband and recovered a further Rs.1 lakh, which had been brought as token payment for taking delivery of Mephedrone. In total, three persons have been arrested in connection with the case. The laboratory setup and procurement of substantial quantities of essential chemicals indicate preparations for significantly expanding the manufacturing capacity. The timely intervention by DRI officers successfully disrupted the plans for any large-scale production . **** SR/KMN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287660) आगंतुक पटल  : 94 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Gujarati Ministry of Finance DRI busts clandestine Mephedrone manufacturing facility in Ankleshwar, Gujarat and seizes Rs. 21 lakh; Three arrested प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: NATIONAL DISASTER MANAGEMENT PLAN
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs NATIONAL DISASTER MANAGEMENT PLAN प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 3:59PM by PIB Delhi The National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) was framed and issued, for the first time, in the year 2016. The plan was revised in the year 2019 in consultation with all stakeholders. The revised NDMP brings together all sectors, ministries and departments at the Central and State level as well as district level functionaries and defines their respective roles and responsibilities in disaster risk reduction. The NDMP has the following main pillars: Conforming to the national legal mandates—the Disaster Management Act, 2005 and the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM) 2009 Participating proactively for realising the global goals as per agreements to which India is signatory—Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and Conference of Parties (COP21), Paris Agreement on Climate Change Prime Minister’s Ten Point Agenda for DRR articulating contemporary national priorities Social inclusion as a ubiquitous and cross-cutting principle Mainstreaming Disaster Risk Reduction is an integral feature of the NDMP. India Disaster Resource Network (IDRN) is a nation-wide electronic inventory of resources that enlists equipment and human resources, collated from districts, states and national level line departments and agencies. IDRN is a web-based platform, for managing the inventory of equipment, skilled human resources and critical supplies for emergency response. Primary focus of IDRN portal is to enable the decision makers to ascertain availability of equipment and human resources required to combat any emergency situation. This database also enables them to assess the level of preparedness for specific disasters and availability of equipment with their location, which can easily be detected and utilized by the needy States/Union Territories/Stakeholders at the time of disasters, to facilitate a quick response. The details of IDRN are available on https://idrn.nidm.gov.in. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha. ***** RK/RR/PS/PR/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287677) आगंतुक पटल  : 54 Ministry of Home Affairs NATIONAL DISASTER MANAGEMENT PLAN प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF NEW CRIMINAL LAWS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs IMPLEMENTATION OF NEW CRIMINAL LAWS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 3:59PM by PIB Delhi The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) came into force throughout the country with effect from 1 July 2024. The States and Union Territories have taken necessary measures for their implementation,  including   issuance   of  relevant   notifications   and  rules, adoption of digital applications and capacity building of stakeholders. Training of police personnel and other State-level stakeholders is primarily undertaken by the respective State and Union Territory Governments. In addition, the Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPR&D) has conducted capacity-building programmes and webinars for Master Trainers and other stakeholders across all 36 States and Union Territories. Since 2024, BPR&D has trained 83,740 officers and stakeholders from the five pillars of the criminal justice system, including Master Trainers. The cadre/position-wise, State/UT-wise and year-wise details are given in Annexure-I. The Master Trainers have also been utilised by State training institutions for conducting further training programmes within the respective States and Union Territories. The details of such training are given in Annexure-II. Further, 110 e-learning courses have been hosted on the iGOT Karmayogi platform, of which 76 courses relate to the new criminal laws. The Nyaya Sanhita provide for the use of technology at various stages of the criminal justice process. Digital systems and applications have been made available for their implementation. These include electronic registration of First Information Reports (e-FIRs), electronic communication and   service   of  summons  (e-Summons),   audio-video  recording  of  search, seizure and investigation proceedings, videography of forensic evidence collection and electronic recording of statements (e-Sakshya), conduct of court proceedings through video conferencing (Nyaya Shruti), MedLeaPR for generating Medical Legal Examination reports and Postmortem reports, Inter Operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) to facilitate electronic exchange of FIRs, charge-sheets and other documents among Police, Courts, Prisons, Prosecution and Forensic Science Laboratories. The deployment and utilisation of these systems are undertaken by the respective States and Union Territories. ‘Police’, and ‘Public Order’ are State-list subjects as per the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. The responsibilities to maintain law and order, protection of life and property of the citizens including investigation and prosecution of crime and criminals rest with the respective State/UT Governments and are competent to deal with such offenses under the extant provisions of law, which also includes the implementation of the Nyaya Sanhita. However, the Central Government supplements their efforts by providing financial support for augmentation of criminal justice infrastructure under various schemes, including the Inter-Operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) 2.0, schemes for modernisation of forensic capacities and Nirbhaya Fund-supported projects. In light of the provisions introduced under the Nyaya Sanhitas, the templates of the data tables have been appropriately modified to ensure consistency, comparability and continuity of the data published in the Crime in India report vis-a-vis data from previous years.                         22 JUL 2026 3:59PM by PIB Delhi The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) came into force throughout the country with effect from 1 July 2024. The States and Union Territories have taken necessary measures for their implementation,  including   issuance   of  relevant   notifications   and  rules, adoption of digital applications and capacity building of stakeholders. Training of police personnel and other State-level stakeholders is primarily undertaken by the respective State and Union Territory Governments. In addition, the Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPR&D) has conducted capacity-building programmes and webinars for Master Trainers and other stakeholders across all 36 States and Union Territories. Since 2024, BPR&D has trained 83,740 officers and stakeholders from the five pillars of the criminal justice system, including Master Trainers. The cadre/position-wise, State/UT-wise and year-wise details are given in Annexure-I. The Master Trainers have also been utilised by State training institutions for conducting further training programmes within the respective States and Union Territories. The details of such training are given in Annexure-II. Further, 110 e-learning courses have been hosted on the iGOT Karmayogi platform, of which 76 courses relate to the new criminal laws. The Nyaya Sanhita provide for the use of technology at various stages of the criminal justice process. Digital systems and applications have been made available for their implementation. These include electronic registration of First Information Reports (e-FIRs), electronic communication and   service   of  summons  (e-Summons),   audio-video  recording  of  search, seizure and investigation proceedings, videography of forensic evidence collection and electronic recording of statements (e-Sakshya), conduct of court proceedings through video conferencing (Nyaya Shruti), MedLeaPR for generating Medical Legal Examination reports and Postmortem reports, Inter Operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) to facilitate electronic exchange of FIRs, charge-sheets and other documents among Police, Courts, Prisons, Prosecution and Forensic Science Laboratories. The deployment and utilisation of these systems are undertaken by the respective States and Union Territories. ‘Police’, and ‘Public Order’ are State-list subjects as per the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. The responsibilities to maintain law and order, protection of life and property of the citizens including investigation and prosecution of crime and criminals rest with the respective State/UT Governments and are competent to deal with such offenses under the extant provisions of law, which also includes the implementation of the Nyaya Sanhita. However, the Central Government supplements their efforts by providing financial support for augmentation of criminal justice infrastructure under various schemes, including the Inter-Operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) 2.0, schemes for modernisation of forensic capacities and Nirbhaya Fund-supported projects. In light of the provisions introduced under the Nyaya Sanhitas, the templates of the data tables have been appropriately modified to ensure consistency, comparability and continuity of the data published in the Crime in India report vis-a-vis data from previous years. title: NATIONAL CYBERCRIME RESPONSE MECHANISM
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs NATIONAL CYBERCRIME RESPONSE MECHANISM प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 3:56PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Home Affairs has set up the ‘Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre’ (I4C) as an attached office to deal with all types of cyber crimes in the country, in a coordinated and comprehensive manner. The ‘National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal’ (NCRP) ( https:// cybercrime.gov.in ) has been launched, as a part of the I4C, to enable public to report incidents pertaining to all types of cyber crimes, with special focus on cyber crimes against women and children. The ‘Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System’ (CFCFRMS), under I4C, has been launched in year 2021 for immediate reporting of financial frauds and to stop siphoning off funds by the fraudsters. As per CFCFRMS operated by I4C, till 30.06.2026, financial amount of more than Rs. 11,158 Crore has been saved in more than 32.80 lakh complaints.  A toll-free Helpline number ‘1930’ has been operationalized to get assistance in lodging online cyber complaints. As per NCRP & CFCFRMS operated by I4C, from the financial years 2023–24 to 2025–26, the total number of cyber fraud complaints on NCRP are more than 5387905, the total number of FIRs registered is more than 181271, the total amount reported is more than ₹ 56087 crores, the total amount marked as  Lien is more than ₹ 9079 crores, and the amount refunded is more than  ₹ 206 crores. Cyber crime incidents reported on National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal , their conversion into FIRs and subsequent action i.e. filing of chargesheets, arrest and resolution of complaints, thereon are handled by the State/UT Law Enforcement Agencies concerned as per the provisions of the law. To further strengthen operational efficiency and ensure uniformity in handling cybercrime complaints, the Ministry has issued a comprehensive Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for NCRP-CFCFRMS. The SOP lays down a  standardized   framework  for   complaint   processing,  bank  coordination, grievance redressal, removal of lien markings, and restoration of defrauded funds to rightful claimants based on complaints received through the NCRP. Money Restoration Module for expeditious restoration of defrauded money to the victims and Grievance Redressal Module for timely attending to the grievances relating to freezing of the bank accounts and lien marking of the amount, have been made functional from April, 2026. The Central Government continuously monitors the average time taken by law enforcement agencies and financial institutions to freeze fraudulently transferred funds. Real time action is ensured through API integration between the CFCFRMS and Financial Institutions for immediately blocking the defrauded amounts. The Central Government has taken the following steps to strengthen inter state coordination and digital forensic capacity : A State of the Art, Cyber Fraud Mitigation Centre (CFMC) has been established at I4C where representatives of major banks, Financial Intermediaries, Payment Aggregators, Telecom Service Providers, IT Intermediaries and representatives of States/UTs Law Enforcement Agency are working together for immediate action and seamless cooperation to tackle cybercrime. Samanvaya Platform has been made operational to serve as an Management Information System (MIS) platform, data repository and a coordination platform for LEAs for cybercrime data sharing and analytics. It provides analytics based interstate linkages of crimes and criminals, involved in cybercrime complaints in various States/UTs. The module ‘Pratibimb’ maps locations of criminals and crime infrastructure on a map to give visibility to jurisdictional officers. The module also facilitates seeking and receiving of techno-legal assistance by Law Enforcement Agencies from I4C and other SMEs. It has lead to arrest of more than 29,837 accused and more than 2,33,593 Cyber Investigation assistance request. ‘Sahyog’ Portal has been launched to expedite the process of sending notices to IT intermediaries by the Appropriate Government or its agency under clause (b) of sub-section (3) of section 79 of the IT Act, 2000 to facilitate the removal or disabling of access to any information, data or communication link being used to commit an unlawful act. A Suspect Registry of identifiers of cyber criminals has been launched by I4C on 10.09.2024 in collaboration with Banks/Financial Institutions. Till 30.06.2026, more than 30.48 lakh suspect identifier data received from Banks and 32.08 lakh Layer 1 mule accounts have been shared with the participating entities of Suspect Registry and declined transactions worth Rs. 25,698 crores. Seven Joint Cyber Coordination Teams (JCCTs) have been constituted for Mewat, Jamtara, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad, Chandigarh, Vishakhapatnam, and Guwahati under I4C covering the whole country based upon cyber crime hotspots/ areas having multi jurisdictional issues by onboarding States/UTs to enhance the coordination framework among the Law Enforcement Agencies of the States/UTs. I4C, MHA is regularly organising ‘State Connect’, ‘Thana Connect’ and Peer learning session to share best practices, enhance capacity building, etc. The state of the art National-Digital Investigation Support Centre (previously known as National Cyber Forensic Laboratory (Investigation)  {NCFL(I)}) has been established, as a part of the I4C, at New Delhi (on 18.02.2019) and at Assam (on 29.08.2025) to provide early stage cyber forensic assistance to Investigating Officers (IOs) of State/UT Police. Till 30.06.2026, National-Digital Investigation Support Centre, New Delhi has provided its services to State/UT LEAs in more than 14,064 cases pertaining to cyber crimes. The Ministry of Home Affairs has released financial assistance  to the tune of Rs. 132.93 crores under the ‘Cyber Crime Prevention against Women and Children (CCPWC)’ Scheme , to the States/UTs for their capacity building such as setting up of cyber forensic-cum-training laboratories, hiring of  junior cyber consultants  and training of  LEAs’ personnel, public prosecutors and judicial officers. Cyber forensic-cum-training laboratories have been commissioned in 33 States/UTs and more than 24,600 LEA personnel, judicial officers and prosecutors have been provided training on cyber crime awareness, investigation, forensics etc. At present, 07 Central Forensic Science Laboratories and 28 State Forensic Science Laboratories are operational across the country to assist in investigation of cybercrime cases. Assistance has been provided to 20 States / UTs inter-alia for Strengthening of Cyber Forensic Capacities in State FSLs under the Nirbhaya funded scheme for Strengthening of DNA Analysis and Cyber Forensic Capacities in State FSLs. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha. ***** RK/RR/PR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287674) आगंतुक पटल  : 28 Ministry of Home Affairs NATIONAL CYBERCRIME RESPONSE MECHANISM प्रविष्टि तिथि:

Seven Joint Cyber Coordination Teams (JCCTs) have been constituted for Mewat, Jamtara, Ahmedabad, Hyderabad, Chandigarh, Vishakhapatnam, and Guwahati under I4C covering the whole country based upon cyber crime hotspots/ areas having multi jurisdictional issues by onboarding States/UTs to enhance the coordination framework among the Law Enforcement Agencies of the States/UTs. I4C, MHA is regularly organising ‘State Connect’, ‘Thana Connect’ and Peer learning session to share best practices, enhance capacity building, etc. The state of the art National-Digital Investigation Support Centre (previously known as National Cyber Forensic Laboratory (Investigation)  {NCFL(I)}) has been established, as a part of the I4C, at New Delhi (on 18.02.2019) and at Assam (on 29.08.2025) to provide early stage cyber forensic assistance to Investigating Officers (IOs) of State/UT Police. Till 30.06.2026, National-Digital Investigation Support Centre, New Delhi has provided its services to State/UT LEAs in more than 14,064 cases pertaining to cyber crimes. The Ministry of Home Affairs has released financial assistance  to the tune of Rs. 132.93 crores under the ‘Cyber Crime Prevention against Women and Children (CCPWC)’ Scheme , to the States/UTs for their capacity building such as setting up of cyber forensic-cum-training laboratories, hiring of  junior cyber consultants  and training of  LEAs’ personnel, public prosecutors and judicial officers. Cyber forensic-cum-training laboratories have been commissioned in 33 States/UTs and more than 24,600 LEA personnel, judicial officers and prosecutors have been provided training on cyber crime awareness, investigation, forensics etc. At present, 07 Central Forensic Science Laboratories and 28 State Forensic Science Laboratories are operational across the country to assist in investigation of cybercrime cases. Assistance has been provided to 20 States / UTs inter-alia for Strengthening of Cyber Forensic Capacities in State FSLs under the Nirbhaya funded scheme for Strengthening of DNA Analysis and Cyber Forensic Capacities in State FSLs. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha. ***** RK/RR/PR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287674)

title: MEASURES TAKEN FOR THE WELFARE OF CAPFS PERSONNEL
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs MEASURES TAKEN FOR THE WELFARE OF CAPFS PERSONNEL प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 3:50PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has taken several measures for welfare of the personnel of the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and their families. These initiatives encompass financial assistance, educational support, housing, and rehabilitation services. Ayushman CAPF: It is an initiative launched by the Government of India under the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) specifically for personnel of the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and their families. It provides cashless and paperless medical treatment at empanelled private and government hospitals across India Ex-Gratia Payments: In the unfortunate event of death due to accidents during duty, CAPF personnel's next of kin receives ₹25 lakh. For deaths resulting from acts of violence by terrorists or during enemy action, the compensation is ₹35 lakh. Accidental death insurance coverage under CAPF salary package scheme : This policy offers financial support to the families of personnel who lose their lives in the line of duty. Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme (PMSS): This scheme has been launched to encourage higher technical and professional education among the wards and widows of CAPF and Assam Rifles personnel. The scheme offers 2,000 scholarships annually (1,000 for boys and 1,000 for girls). The scholarship amounts are ₹3,000 per month for girls and ₹2,500 per month for boys, disbursed annually as ₹36,000 and ₹30,000, respectively. Contributory Welfare Fund :- Necessary guidelines has been issued to bring uniformity in payout to the Next of Kins (NoKs) of deceased CAPF personnel from Contributory Welfare Fund. Quota for wards of CAPF :- 26 seats in MBBS & 03 seats in BDS have been reserved for the wards of serving/deceased CAPFs & AR personnel. CAPF e-Awas Portal: A dedicated online platform has been developed which facilitates the registration and allotment of residential quarters to CAPF personnel.  It also provides facility for inter-force allotment. Welfare and Rehabilitation Board (WARB): This has been established to oversee the welfare and rehabilitation of retired CAPF personnel and their families, including the next of kin of deceased or disabled personnel. WARB operates through State and District Welfare Officers across the country. “CAPF Punarvaas” scheme: - A “CAPF Punarvaas” scheme was launched by linking Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act (PSARA) website with WARB website where the data of retired and willing Ex-CAPF/AR personnel is made available to Private Security Agencies on PSARA website for re-employment in Private Security Agencies. Medical Facilities: Retired personnel and their spouses receive medical facilities from CGHS/CPMF Hospitals or a medical allowance of ₹1000 per month. Risk and Hardship Allowance: Risk and Hardship allowance is being provided for CAPF personnel deployed in Jammu and Kashmir, Left-Wing Extremism affected districts & North Eastern States. Kendriya Police Kalyan Bhandar (KPKB): The government has introduced 50% GST concession to the beneficiaries on purchase of Goods from KPKB, w.e.f 01.04.2024 to provide quality products to CAPF personnel at discounted rates . Liberalized Pension Awards (LPA) and Extraordinary Family Pension (EFP ): There are special pension schemes designed for the families of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel who suffer death or disability due to operational hazards, ensuring financial security for their dependents. Bharat Ke Veer: It is an initiative launched by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to support the families of deceased Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel. It enables citizens to contribute financially to the families of soldiers who have sacrificed their lives in the line of duty. Operational Casualty Certificate :  CAPF personnel killed in action or on duty  gets  ‘Operational   Casualty  Certificate’  on   the   line  of  ‘Battle Casualty Certificate’ as available to Armed Forces.  NoKs are entitled to certain benefits viz Air and Rail travel fare concession and allotment of Oil Product Agencies. Compassionate Appointment : Compassionate Appointment is also given to the eligible dependent in accordance with the Government instructions. Honorary Rank : To boost the self-esteem and sense of pride among the personnel, Honorary Rank is being granted to the personnel (Constable to Sub-inspector) of CAPFs & Assam Rifles, w.e.f 23.05.2025. Air Courier Service : Air travel facility is provided to entitled CAPFs & AR  personnel deployed in Kashmir Valley. Additional HRA : Sanction of additional HRA at the rate of ‘Y’ Class city (20% of basic pay) to the CAPF personnel posted in Kashmir Valley for keeping their families at last place of posting, if retention of Government accommodation has not been availed. Bus Services for the wards of CAPFs personn el - School bus facility is provided to the wards of CAPFs & Assam Rifles personnel deployed in J&K, LWE and North Eastern States. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha. ***** RK/RR/PR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287666) आगंतुक पटल  : 29 Ministry of Home Affairs MEASURES TAKEN FOR THE WELFARE OF CAPFS PERSONNEL प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: DEVELOPMENT IN LEFT WING EXTREMISM AFFECTED DISTRICTS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs DEVELOPMENT IN LEFT WING EXTREMISM AFFECTED DISTRICTS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 3:49PM by PIB Delhi To address the LWE menace holistically, a ‘National Policy and Action Plan to address LWE’ was approved in 2015. It envisages a multi-pronged strategy involving security related measures, development interventions, ensuring rights and entitlements of local communities etc. In line with the policy and to give impetus to the development of the erstwhile most LWE affected districts funds are provided for filling critical gaps in  public  infrastructure under  ‘Special Central Assistance (SCA)  Scheme’.  Till  now,  approximately  ₹4282.96  crores  have been released to the States since the inception of the Scheme in 2017. In addition to this Scheme, several LWE affected areas specific initiatives have been taken with special thrust on expansion of road network, improving telecommunication connectivity, education, skill development and financial inclusion. A few of these initiatives undertaken on development front are enumerated below: For expansion of road network, 15189 km have been constructed under 02 LWE   specific schemes namely Road Requirement Plan (RRP) and Road Connectivity Project for LWE Affected Areas (RCPLWEA). For improving telecom connectivity in LWE affected areas 9497 towers have been commissioned. For Skill Development, 47 Industrial Training Institute (ITI) and 49 Skill Development Centres (SDC) have been opened. For quality education in tribal areas 179 Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS) have been made functional. For financial inclusion, Department of Posts has opened 6,025 Post Offices with banking services in LWE affected districts. 1804 Bank Branches and 1321 ATMs have been opened in Most LWE affected districts. As a result of resolute implementation of the policy entire country has been liberated from LWE. The consolidated gains achieved through sustained security and development efforts have created favorable environment for comprehensive socio - economic transformation of the regions that were affected by LWE for decades. This was stated by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Home Affairs Shri Nityanand Rai in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha. ***** RK/RR/PR/PS/SC (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287663) आगंतुक पटल  : 26 Ministry of Home Affairs DEVELOPMENT IN LEFT WING EXTREMISM AFFECTED DISTRICTS प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Government Supports Indian Filmmakers through Financial Assistance, International Partnerships and Global Promotion
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Government Supports Indian Filmmakers through Financial Assistance, International Partnerships and Global Promotion A High-Level Study Group also Constituted to Further Examine Opportunities and Challenges in the Indian Film Sector प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 4:15PM by PIB Delhi Under the Development, Communication and Dissemination of Filmic Content (DCDFC) Scheme, the Government provides financial assistance for the production of regional films. These initiatives benefit filmmakers across the country, including those from Maharashtra, and contribute to strengthening India's film ecosystem and enhancing its global competitiveness. The Government has also undertaken several initiatives to strengthen the Indian film ecosystem and enhance the global outreach of Indian cinema. Through the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC), financial assistance is provided to such filmmakers. To facilitate international promotion and market access, the Government supports the participation of Indian filmmakers at major international film festivals and film markets. The Ministry also collaborates with industry bodies such as The Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) and International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) to promote Indian cinema and create opportunities for international partnerships. In addition, financial assistance is provided to Indian Missions abroad for organising activities aimed at promoting Indian cinema and facilitating engagement between Indian and international film industries. Such initiatives include the WAVES Bazaar, Work-in-Progress Labs, Viewing Rooms, film markets, and programmes for facilitating international coproductions. These platforms provide project development support, networking opportunities, and international market access to Indian Filmmakers. Maharashtra continues to be one of the country's leading film production hubs, with worldclass infrastructure and facilities. Dadasaheb Phalke Chitranagari (Film City), Goregaon is located in Mumbai. Institutes like the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, and Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT), Mumbai support capacity building of the sector. Apart from these, a wide network of production and post-production facilities by private sector is also functioning across Mumbai, Pune and Nashik. To further examine the issues related to film sector, the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has recently constituted a High-Level Study Group. Based on the report of this Group, further policy interventions will be formulated. This information was provided by the Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, in a written reply to an Unstarred Question in the Lok Sabha raised by Dr. Amol Ramsing Kolhe. **** Mahesh Kumar/ Vivek Vishwash (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287703) आगंतुक पटल  : 35 Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Government Supports Indian Filmmakers through Financial Assistance, International Partnerships and Global Promotion A High-Level Study Group also Constituted to Further Examine Opportunities and Challenges in the Indian Film Sector प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Draft Telecommunications (Television, Radio and Associated Services) Rules, 2026 to Simplify Regulatory Framework for Television and Radio Services
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Draft Telecommunications (Television, Radio and Associated Services) Rules, 2026 to Simplify Regulatory Framework for Television and Radio Services Single Rule Book Proposed to Streamline Compliance and Enhance Ease of Doing Business for Broadcasters Draft Rules Provide Existing Licensees Flexibility to Opt for Voluntary Migration or Continue Under Existing Licences/Permissions until Migration प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi The Government has released the draft Telecommunications (Television, Radio and Associated Services) Rules, 2026 to consolidate the various Guidelines issued for Television and Radio services, within the framework of the newly enacted Telecommunications Act, 2023. The following Guidelines have been integrated into this set of rules: Policy Guidelines for Uplinking and Downlinking of Satellite Television Channels in India; Guidelines for obtaining a license to provide Direct-to-Home (DTH) Broadcasting Services in India; Guidelines for providing Headend-in-the-Sky (HITS) Broadcasting Services in India; Policy Guidelines on Expansion of FM Radio Broadcasting Services through Private Agencies (Phase III); Revised Policy Guidelines for setting up Community Radio Stations in India; and Guidelines for provisioning of Internet Protocol Television (IPTV) Services. With this set of rules, the industry will now have a unified and significantly simplified rule book. These rules are designed to harmonize the existing regime while promoting ease of doing business in the Television and Radio broadcasting sector. The draft rules have been published on the website of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting ( https://www.mib.gov.in/ ), inviting inputs, comments or suggestions by the 27 th July 2026. To support industry transition to new regulatory framework, the draft rules provide for voluntary migration of existing licenses/permission to the new authorisation framework or continuation of existing licences/permission until migration. The draft rules contain provisions to improve availability of Television and Radio services, including community radio services, across the country, including remote and rural areas of Chhindwara district, Madhya Pradesh. This information was provided by Union Minister of Railways, Information and Broadcasting and Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw to a starred question in the Lok Sabha raised by Shri Mukeshkumar Chandrakaant Dalal and Shri Dineshbhai Makwana. **** Mahesh Kumar/ Vivek Vishwash (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287670) आगंतुक पटल  : 69 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Gujarati , Kannada Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Draft Telecommunications (Television, Radio and Associated Services) Rules, 2026 to Simplify Regulatory Framework for Television and Radio Services Single Rule Book Proposed to Streamline Compliance and Enhance Ease of Doing Business for Broadcasters Draft Rules Provide Existing Licensees Flexibility to Opt for Voluntary Migration or Continue Under Existing Licences/Permissions until Migration प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: 50 OTT Platforms Disabled in Last Two Years for Displaying Obscene Content and Violations of IT Act and Other Applicable Laws
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 50 OTT Platforms Disabled in Last Two Years for Displaying Obscene Content and Violations of IT Act and Other Applicable Laws प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 3:15PM by PIB Delhi Government has notified the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media, Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 on 25.02.2021 under IT Act, 2000 to put in place an institutional mechanism for publishers of current affairs on digital media and publishers of online curated content (OTT Platforms). Part-III of the rules provides for a Code of Ethics for digital news publishers and publishers of online curated content (OTT platforms). Complaints are addressed under the provisions of the IT Rules, 2021. Section 79(3)(b) of IT Act, 2000 provides for notification to the intermediaries for removing/disabling access to unlawful content. Based on complaints, the Government regularly takes action against such intermediaries and OTT platforms. The Government has disabled 50 OTT platforms for public access in India in last two years for displaying obscene content and for violation of Section 67 and 67A of the IT Act, Section 294 of the BNS, and Section 4 of the Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act, 1986. This information was provided by the Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs Dr. L. Murugan, in a written reply to a question raised by Shri Rajabhau Parag Prakash Waje in the Lok Sabha today. **** Mahesh Kumar/Aparajita Priyadarshini (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287639) आगंतुक पटल  : 184 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Gujarati , Kannada Ministry of Information & Broadcasting 50 OTT Platforms Disabled in Last Two Years for Displaying Obscene Content and Violations of IT Act and Other Applicable Laws प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: WAVES Film Bazaar Screenwriters' Lab 2025 project ‘Yayavar – The Migrating Bird’ signs Letter of Intent for international collaboration
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Information & Broadcasting WAVES Film Bazaar Screenwriters' Lab 2025 project ‘Yayavar – The Migrating Bird’ signs Letter of Intent for international collaboration Project developed under the Screenwriters’ Lab enters into a partnership with Finland-based production house for development, financing, production and international positioning प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 1:05PM by PIB Mumbai WAVES Film Bazaar, organised by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) under the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Government of India, has announced that “Yayavar – The Migrating Bird”, a project selected for the WAVES Film Bazaar Screenwriters’ Lab 2025, has signed a Letter of Intent (LOI) for an international collaboration. The project has entered into a partnership with iRoller Media & Entertainment (India), and Norse Key Productions (Finland), to jointly develop, finance, produce and position the film for international audiences. Under the Letter of Intent, iRoller Media & Entertainment will serve as Lead Producer, leading financing, production planning and execution, while Norse Key Productions will lead and facilitate post-production activities in Finland and support the project’s international outreach and festival positioning. The collaboration reflects the growing impact of the WAVES Film Bazaar Screenwriters’ Lab in nurturing promising Indian screenwriting talent and creating meaningful opportunities for global collaboration. title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF PANCHAYATI RAJ INSTITUTIONS (PRI)
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Panchayati Raj DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF PANCHAYATI RAJ INSTITUTIONS (PRI) प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 4:25PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP) under the Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) with the objective of strengthening transparency, efficiency, and accountability in the functioning of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) through digital enablement across all States. eGramSwaraj and AuditOnline are applications developed under the e-Panchayat MMP and are being implemented across Gram Panchayats throughout the country to strengthen transparency, accountability and digital governance in Panchayati Raj Institutions. eGramSwaraj facilitates planning, budgeting, accounting, progress reporting and asset management, while AuditOnline enables online auditing of Panchayat accounts in accordance with the prescribed audit framework. As on date, during the FY 2025–26, out of a total of 2,58,730 Gram Panchayats and equivalent across the States/UTs, 2,55,251 Gram Panchayats and equivalent (98.65%), have uploaded their Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) on e-Gram Swaraj and 2,45,839 Gram Panchayats and equivalents (95%) have made payments amounting to ₹57,337 crore through the e-GramSwaraj–PFMS interface. Further for audit period 2024-25, audit report for 2,33,743 GPs have been generated. Additionally, integration of eGramSwaraj with platforms such as GeM, BSNL and BHASHINI, along with weather information services, has further improved transparency, accessibility and informed decision-making at the grassroots level. Furthermore, Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a State subject and part of the State list of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. However, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of revamped Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) since the financial year 2022-23 in States/ UTs. With the objectives to strengthen the capacity of Panchayati Raj institutions (PRIs) by imparting training to Elected Representatives (ERs), Panchayat Functionaries and other stakeholders to develop their governance capabilities for leadership roles, enabling the Gram Panchayats to function effectively, across all States/UTs. Under the scheme of RGSA, the Ministry provides support for Capacity Building & Training (CB&T) of elected representatives, functionaries and other stakeholders of Panchayats in different categories including various digital trainings as per the priority of the States/UTs. Since, 2023-24 to 2026-27 (as on 10.07.2026), 3,73,422 elected representatives and Panchayat officials have been trained on e-Governance and other digital platforms. The applications developed under the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project (MMP), namely eGramSwaraj, Meri Panchayat, Panchayat NIRNAY, AuditOnline and SabhaSaar, promote transparency and accountability by providing public access to Panchayat information, facilitating transparent Gram Sabha proceedings, enabling online audit of Panchayat accounts, and supporting AI-enabled documentation of meetings. Further, the Ministry is encouraging Panchayats to adopt their own Citizens’ Charter for effective delivery of services. 30 States/UTs are delivering online citizen services at the Grassroot including Birth and Death Certificates, Marriage Registration, Caste, Income, Residence, Age, Character and Disability Certificates, pension-related services, land and property-related services, water and sanitation services, grievance redressal, and applications under various welfare schemes. This has improved the accessibility, transparency and efficiency of citizen service delivery at the grassroots level, thereby enhancing the quality of life and ease of living for rural citizens. Under the e-Panchayat Mission Mode Project, funds are being provided to National Informatics Centre Services Inc. (NICSI) for central-level support towards maintenance of e-Panchayat applications. No funds are being released to the States/UTs. Fund released under e-Panchayat MMP during last three years and the current year is as under: Rs. in crore Year BE RE Actuals 2023-24 20.00 16.28 16.03 2024-25 90.17 34.00 13.47 2025-26 20.00 20.00 20.00 2026-27 30.00 - 6.42 The details of funds that were released to the States/UTs for purchase and strengthening of digital governance initiatives across Panchayati Raj Institutions under the Revamped RGSA are given below: Rs. in crore 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 2026-27 (upto 10.07.2026) Annual Action Plan (AAP) Approved Funds Released AAP Approved Funds Released AAP Approved Funds Released AAP Approved Funds Released 4844.06 800.17 4307.41 670.40 4817.27 768.13 AAP for FY 2026-27 has not been considered so far 215.35 For FY 2025–26, the releases comprise funds through both SNA till 30 th June 2025 and SNA-SPARSH since 1 st July 2025. content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Panchayati Raj FINANCE COMMISSION GRANTS TO PANCHAYATI RAJ INSTITUTIONS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 4:22PM by PIB Delhi State-wise details of the grants released under the 15 th Finance Commission to the Rural Local Bodies in 28 states, including Andhra Pradesh, for the year 2021-26 are given at Annexure. Unreleased amount represents grants that could not be released during the award period due to non-fulfilment of the prescribed eligibility conditions by the concerned State Governments / Rural Local Bodies (RLBs). Once the recommendations of the Finance Commission, which is a constitutional body, are accepted by the Government and are laid before the Parliament, the same cannot be altered. Panchayat, being “Local Self Government”, is a state subject. However, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj promotes decentralized planning and effective implementation of development works through the Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP) framework. Gram Panchayats prepare and upload their GPDPs on the eGramSwaraj portal, which serves as a comprehensive digital platform for planning, budgeting, accounting, and monitoring of Panchayat activities. The preparation of GPDPs is undertaken annually through a participatory process involving Gram Sabhas, and the plans include works and activities to be implemented through the convergence of various Central and State schemes. This report presents the Devolution Index, which provides the overall scores and ranks for all States/Union Territories covered under Part-IX of the Constitution, based on six identified dimensions: Framework, Functions, Finances, Functionaries, Capacity Enhancement, and Accountability. title: NeVA Sewa Kendras have been established in 22 Legislative Houses
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs NeVA Sewa Kendras have been established in 22 Legislative Houses प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 2:26PM by PIB Delhi As of now, National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA) Sewa Kendras (e-Facilitation Centres) have been established in 22 Legislative Houses. Under the Capacity Building component of the NeVA project, comprehensive orientation workshops and handholding support are provided to stakeholders of all on boarded Legislatures to familiarize them with the functionalities of NeVA. Recently, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs delivered a session on NeVA to the newly elected Members of the West Bengal Legislative Assembly at Kolkata on 04.07.2026. The NeVA Public Portal, available in 23 languages, provides citizens with online access to legislative business, including Bills, Questions, Proceedings and other legislative documents of Legislatures on boarded on the NeVA platform. As such, having multilingual support, the portal is being widely used by the public to access legislative information. This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) of Law and Justice and Minister of State of Parliamentary Affairs, Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal in a written reply in Lok Sabha today. *** ISA (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287617) आगंतुक पटल  : 130 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs NeVA Sewa Kendras have been established in 22 Legislative Houses प्रविष्टि तिथि:
